A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cardinal revealed-preferences axiom AE is superior to the ordinal revealed-preferences axiom WARP and is as predictive as the rationality assumption GARP.
the AE axiom is the best predictor for consumer behavior in finite environments, and that it can be rationalized by means of a utility function that is consistent in a natural sense.

The main takeaway from our work is that

cardinal revealed preference, which is a natural extension of the ordinal notion of revealed preference, provides a new way of understanding consumer behavior that is both theoretically and practically appealing.
cardinal preferences, as opposed to binary choice, can be used to explain consumer behavior.
cardinal preferences, which are the standard tool for consumer theory and welfare economics, are not only consistent with the observed data but are also the best way to explain the data.
